As Vivienne spoke, she squeezed Elijah’s hand, like meeting me had wronged him in the worst way.

Elijah’s face stayed cold, unreadable.

But I was so furious my vision almost blurred. I wanted to slap this fake ingénue across the face.

What kind of shamelessness did it take to frame someone so calmly, without even blinking?

The entire Turner family was blind, fooled by her sweet, rotten act.

The cop looked doubtful. "Is that so?"

Vivienne asked, "Other than the phone, you didn’t find any other leads, right?"

"Not at the moment," the cop said.

"Exactly." Vivienne sighed. "She dropped her phone on purpose, left a little clue, just to make everyone worry.

I really didn’t expect that after all these years, she still hasn’t grown out of this disappearing habit.

But she’ll come back."

The cop frowned. "Why are you so sure?"

Vivienne smiled. "Because in a few days it’s Great-Grandpa’s ninetieth birthday banquet. Our Turner family is throwing a big, glamorous party. Great-Grandpa loves my sister the most—his oldest great-granddaughter. No matter how much she pouts, she’ll come back to celebrate his birthday."

Tears fell from me without warning.

Vivienne wasn’t wrong. In the Turner family, the one who loved me most was Great-Grandpa.

This fake ingénue stole everything from me—but she never stole my place in Great-Grandpa’s heart. Too bad he was already so old. He loved me, but sometimes he was clear, sometimes he was confused. When it came to the younger generation’s mess, he was powerless.

A few days ago, when he was lucid, he called me and talked about his birthday.

"Yas, Great-Grandpa lives one day at a time. This might be the last time I get to celebrate a full birthday.

You have to come back and celebrate with me."

"Okay, Great-Grandpa. I’ll definitely come back to celebrate you," I’d promised.

But now… I was going to break that promise.

I was already dead. I could never go back to wish him happy birthday.

"She’s probably hiding somewhere, watching everyone run around in circles for her," Vivienne added viciously. "She’s probably secretly thrilled."

After listening to Vivienne’s whole performance, Elijah stood up. "Crimes happen every day. I hope the police don’t waste resources on a spoiled young lady’s boring game.

And certainly not my time.

This Ms. Turner has nothing to do with me."

Seeing how cold he was, the cop didn’t say much more. "Alright. We’ll contact the Turner family and investigate."

"On Great-Grandpa’s birthday banquet day, my sister will definitely come back." As they left the station, Vivienne reassured Elijah again, so confident it sounded like a vow.

But after Elijah drove Vivienne home, he stayed alone in the car for a long time.

He picked up his phone again and again. In the end, he narrowed his eyes and said harshly, "Yasmine, you’d better not show up at that banquet."

He looked vicious, like if I showed up, it would mean his worry had been wasted—and he’d strangle me for it.

Fine.

I wouldn’t disappoint him.

I was dead. I couldn’t possibly appear at Great-Grandpa’s birthday banquet two days later.

And yet—when my soul opened its eyes, I was at the banquet resort.

Maybe heaven took pity on me, letting me wish Great-Grandpa happy birthday one last time.

The resort was lit up and decorated, packed with guests. Loud. Festive.

Ninety was a milestone birthday. Of course the Turner family had to throw it big.

I floated in the air, watching Great-Grandpa in his traditional tunic, kind-faced and gentle. Warmth filled me… and so did grief.

I never expected that phone call would be my goodbye.

When it was the great-grandchildren’s turn, it was Vivienne who carried the tea over to celebrate him.

She replaced me again—me, the oldest great-granddaughter.

That real heiress is nothing…"

And all I ever received was contempt.

Especially Logan—he kept shaking Elijah’s hand and wouldn’t let go, smiling so hard his face almost cracked. "Young Master Foster, your presence at Great-Grandpa’s birthday banquet really adds so much glory to the whole event."

If it were only the Turner family, their wealth and status in front of Elijah didn’t even count as small fries.

With Vivienne engaged to Elijah, the Turners had finally latched onto a true top-tier family.

Great-Grandpa accepted it happily. "Thank you, Young Master Foster."

Next, it was Vivienne’s turn to offer tea.

Holding the teacup, she knelt in front of Great-Grandpa. "Great-Grandpa, your great-granddaughter Vivienne wishes you endless blessings and a long life."

Even though he no longer ran Turner Enterprises, in the family he still held the highest status.

The moment he got angry, the entire atmosphere turned colder.

No one cared about my disappearance.

My body should’ve already started to stink.

The tone he used was like he was talking about a stranger.

The one stepping on me was my aunt, Judith Turner.

Insulting me wasn’t enough. She had to praise Vivienne too. "And it was that time she almost ruined my big brother’s project. Luckily Vivienne saved the day. Otherwise the Turner family would’ve lost a huge deal.

Vivienne is beautiful and talented. If Yasmine were even half as capable, she’d bring the Turners some pride."

"Please. Forget bringing pride. It’d be good enough if she didn’t embarrass the family." The voice came from Jennifer, Uncle James’s wife. "I heard she’s been working at a club lately…"

She didn’t finish before Georgia cut her off. "What day is it? Don’t bring up filthy things."

It was Great-Grandpa’s milestone birthday. So many guests. She hated me, but she didn’t want to air dirty laundry in public.

Jennifer shut up.

"What club?" Great-Grandpa had heard it anyway. His voice dropped, heavy with anger. "What kind of filth are you smearing on Yas?"

"Grandpa, Yasmine is your favorite. Who would dare smear her?" Judith hurried to smooth things over. Seeing Vivienne still kneeling, she reminded him, "Grandpa, Vivienne’s arms are getting tired. Just take the tea already."

"That’s right. Drink Vivienne’s longevity tea." Second Uncle James chimed in. "Yasmine is just throwing a little fit. It’s not worth getting angry over."

Great-Grandpa suddenly looked at Vivienne. Angry, he lifted his hand and pointed his cane at her, scolding, "Vivienne—did you hide Yas again?"

Elijah, who’d been silent the whole time, lifted a brow.

Chapter 6: How Could He Miss Me?
Vivienne’s face flashed with shock. She shook her head fast. “Great-Grandpa, how could I hide my sister—”

Great-Grandpa cut her off. “Last time, it was you who locked Yas in the attic and made everyone think she was throwing a tantrum and hiding on purpose. You lied to Yas, lured her up there, and locked her in, just so you could steal her chance to perform at City Hall.

“This time, what kind of scheme are you playing now?”

Great-Grandpa demanded, furious.

Vivienne looked innocent and terrified. Her eyes reddened in an instant. Even the hands holding her teacup were trembling. “Great-Grandpa, it wasn’t me.”

“Dad, don’t be mad. Why bring up old stuff?” Georgia hurried to support Great-Grandpa. “Vivienne is so sweet and well-behaved. How could it possibly be her who locked that dead girl in the attic?

“Don’t go believing rumors.”

“It was her!” Great-Grandpa glared at Vivienne. “Yas told me herself. You locked her in the attic. Other people don’t believe it, but I do.”

My eyes burned hot.

Great-Grandpa was so angry he suddenly jabbed his cane down onto the cup.

The cup fell to the floor and shattered. Tea splashed all over Vivienne.

I saw it—so fast it was almost nothing—a cold glint sliding through Vivienne’s eyes. But she pretended to shake in fear, tears spilling as she whimpered, “Great-Grandpa, it really wasn’t me.”

That pitiful, delicate look made Logan ache for her. He immediately stepped in to protect Vivienne. “Grandpa, Vivienne has been good and sensible since she was a kid. How could she lock Yasmine in the attic? You can’t just listen to one side.

“Yasmine’s always had a temper. She plays disappearance games—”

“Shut up!” Great-Grandpa lifted his cane and struck Logan across the back. “No matter how much Yas throws a tantrum, she would never skip my birthday banquet. Something must’ve happened to her—that’s the only reason she broke her word.

“Logan, Yas is your daughter. Don’t let your mind get clogged with grease and end up pitying the wrong person.

“Get to the police station right now and find out what’s going on with Yas.”

Great-Grandpa barked the order.

Seeing the Old Master truly furious, Logan answered again and again, “Yes, yes, Grandpa. I’m going right now.”

Logan left the longevity hall. Georgia immediately lowered her voice to Elijah. “Young Master Foster, the Old Master’s a little confused. Please don’t take it to heart.”

“Yes, yes. After all, he’s ninety,” Uncle James chimed in.

They were terrified Elijah would believe it, form a bad impression of Vivienne, and ruin the engagement.

Elijah said nothing, his attitude unreadable.

Vivienne lowered her head and cried softly, looking wronged. At a time like this, acting innocent was stronger than anything she could say.

After Logan went out, he didn’t go to the police station at all. He called his assistant over and told him to pass a message to my mom. “Tell Helen to find Yasmine right away. Tell her not to cause trouble for the Turner family!”

Trouble.

So I was his trouble.

I’d known for a long time I didn’t matter in his heart, but hearing those words out loud still hurt like hell.

In the entire Turner family, only Great-Grandpa had ever truly loved me.

I knelt on the floor and knocked my head three times, hard.

I’m sorry, Great-Grandpa. I can’t stay alive to wish you longevity, but you have to live a long, long life.

It was like Great-Grandpa felt my blessing. He lifted his head and looked toward where I was kneeling, his eyes turning wet. He sighed, propping himself up with his cane. “All of you… you’re all blind.”

Then he pointed at Vivienne, still kneeling on the floor. “If you dare stir up trouble again, heaven will take you. Keep kneeling.”

Vivienne bit her lip lightly, wearing the obedient, dutiful face of someone falsely accused yet not daring to argue.

But her eyes were dark with chill.

She’d brought Elijah here to celebrate longevity, wanting to show off in front of the guests. Instead, Great-Grandpa had smashed the teacup and punished her on her knees.

Great-Grandpa had no mood to accept any more birthday wishes. He left the longevity hall.

The guests followed. After everyone dispersed, Elijah finally helped Vivienne up.

Vivienne sniffled softly and looked at Elijah with wounded eyes. “Elijah… do you not believe me either?”

Elijah paused, then looked at her. “That day at the police station, you were so sure Yasmine would come back. But today she didn’t.”

Vivienne hurried to explain, “I don’t know why she didn’t come back either. Great-Grandpa loves her most. Logically, she would definitely come back to wish him a happy birthday. But she’s still being stubborn. This time, my sister really has no sense of boundaries.

“Even if she’s heartbroken from a breakup, she can’t let Great-Grandpa down.”

I narrowed my eyes.

What a fake ingénue. Even while scrubbing herself clean, she still found time to splash a bucket of filth all over me.

Elijah didn’t speak.

Vivienne hooked her arm through his. “Elijah, don’t worry about my sister for now. She’s probably just too hurt, hiding a little longer this time. The banquet’s starting. Let’s go over. You’re the main guest, and later you have to go onstage to give Great-Grandpa a birthday speech.”

Elijah lifted his lips. The word “okay” hadn’t even left his mouth when his phone rang.

After glancing at the caller ID showing the police station, Elijah answered. “Hello.”

“Hello, Mr. Foster. This is Officer Walters from the Millbrook Police Station. There’s a new development in Yasmine’s case. It’s somewhat related to you. Mr. Foster, could you come to the station and cooperate with the investigation?”

“Sure,” Elijah agreed, crisp and immediate.

A cold gleam flashed through Vivienne’s eyes, but her voice stayed sweet with concern. “Is there new progress in my sister’s case?”

Elijah didn’t hide it. “Yeah. I’m heading to the station now.”

“I’ll go with you.”

Elijah refused at first. “I’ll handle the case. The banquet is about to start. You stay and eat with Great-Grandpa, or he’ll get unhappy again.”

“Elijah, you saw it. Great-Grandpa is really worried about my sister. If I go handle my sister’s situation, he won’t be unhappy.” Vivienne’s face was full of concern. “And I’m worried about her too. I want to know what new clues the police found.”

At the police station.

I drifted into the reception room ahead of Vivienne and Elijah.

I saw my cousin, Cameron Shaw. He was telling the officer, “My aunt is sick and can’t get out of bed. I came in her place. Officer, what’s the new lead?”

My heart clenched.

I’d been missing for five days. Mom must’ve been so devastated she’d gotten sick.

“We’ll go look once Mr. Foster arrives,” the officer said.

Cameron’s tone turned heavy. “Does the clue have something to do with Elijah?”

“It’s a little…” The officer stopped mid-sentence and smiled, nodding toward behind Cameron. “Mr. Foster, you’re here.”

Cameron turned around.

Vivienne had her arm linked with Elijah’s, the two of them walking in as a pair.

Seeing that sick display of closeness, Cameron’s face instantly darkened with rage. He strode up in a few big steps, stopping right in front of Elijah. “Elijah, you sanctimonious hypocrite! Yas gave you everything, and this is how you treat her!

“When she comes back, you will apologize to her!”

Elijah let out a cold laugh, mocking Cameron’s anger like it was nothing but cheap posturing. They were both tall, solid men, but Elijah’s shadow covered Cameron with a pressure that felt born into his bones.

“Want me to apologize to her?” Elijah’s voice was icy. “Then let her crawl to my feet and beg for forgiveness first.”

My heart ripped in two.

I’d been good to him in every way. I even sold my blood to buy him medicine—and I still had to beg him for forgiveness?

text:
I was sliced open by a thug and died in a filthy gutter.

That day was supposed to be the day my boyfriend proposed to me. Instead, he slid a two hundred million dollar diamond ring onto my stepsister’s finger.

Only in that moment did I understand who the breathtaking man in front of me really was—Elijah Foster, CEO of Foster Holdings, the kind of man who could turn international finance upside down with a flick of his hand.

But when we first met, he told me he was dirt poor—an Uber driver with liver disease, barely staying alive on imported meds.

To scrape together money for those “life-saving” pills, I worked package delivery during the day, rode deliveries until my legs shook, and spent nights in clubs pouring drinks. I even sold my blood more than once, just to buy time for him—until the day he could get a liver transplant.

And then, the day I showed up excited, dressed nicely, imported meds in hand, I discovered the truth.

Everything was a performance. And my love was the joke.

My whole body shook. My lipstick couldn’t hide how pale my lips were. While Elijah looked at my stepsister with a tenderness that made the room sigh, I stood there swallowing the ridicule, the contempt, becoming a punchline for the upper class.

The insults were unbearable. Elijah didn’t just watch coldly—he took the ridiculously expensive imported pills I’d just bought with blood money and tossed them to the floor one by one, like they were trash. His words were even colder.

“One hundred thousand dollars a bottle. For a poor nobody like you, I’m sure that sounds like a fortune. But Yasmine Turner, do you know something? The pharmaceutical company that makes that drug belongs to me. Elijah Foster.”

His mouth curved, a devil’s tease in the smile.

My heart hurt so badly I couldn’t even breathe through it. I couldn’t understand why he’d pretended to be broke just to toy with some Cinderella like me.

I clenched my fists and charged forward. Ignoring the shocked stares from those wealthy wives and heiresses, I grabbed the collar of Elijah’s expensive suit and yanked him toward me.

“Elijah! You lied to get my money, you lied to get my blood, you lied to get my heart! Watching me grind like a dog for scraps every day—did that make you feel proud?!”

He clearly hadn’t expected me to do that. The eyes that had once pretended to be gentle and harmless now held only amused superiority.

He glanced at the bodyguards. Those hulking men immediately dragged me off him.

Before I was taken away, I wiped my tears and screamed, “You don’t deserve my love!”

His bodyguards shoved me out of the room—then actually threw me off the yacht, straight into the hands of the thug who came to take my life.

In the last few minutes before everything went dark, instead of calling the police, I called the man I had poured every feeling I had into.

Even though my sincerity had been fed to the dogs, deep down I still clung to a sliver of luck about human nature. I still wanted to believe he might reach out a hand and save me.

“Elijah, save me. Someone’s chasing—”

“Yasmine, know your place and get lost,” the man cut me off, cold and ruthless. “Or I’ll make sure you can’t survive in Ashbourne.”

I froze.

The thug wanted me dead, and Elijah wanted me unable to live.

And I was still begging him for help.

My heart felt like it was being carved apart. I bit my lip until I tasted blood, my voice shaking out of key. “Elijah… why are you doing this to me?”

“Why?” Elijah mocked. “Yasmine, do you know what the cheapest thing in the world is?”

I didn’t answer.

His voice was light, contemptuous, vicious. “The sincerity of shameless poor people like you.”

Something inside me exploded into a gaping hole. Blood surged through it. The pain was so violent I forgot to run.

Then my stepsister Vivienne Langley’s sweet, understanding voice floated through the phone. “Elijah, don’t do that to my sister. She was so good to you. If she sold her body, she must’ve been forced to…”

Sold my body?

I didn’t even have time to process what that fake innocent was implying before Elijah’s icy disdain swept in like a blade.

“A bottom-feeding insect doesn’t deserve to call you sister. Watch your filthy mouth.”

I couldn’t stop shaking anymore. Finally, I snapped, hysterical. “Elijah, you’re the one who hid your identity and played with my feelings—so why are you acting like some judge, trampling me like you’re righteous?!”

Heh.

Elijah gave a cold laugh. His voice had no emotion as it sliced into my ear. “Yasmine, when you’re dead, I’ll tell you at your grave.”

He wanted me dead.

My whole body jolted like I’d been thrown into deep winter. The phone slipped from my hand, hit the sharp edge of a rock, and shattered into pieces.

The thug who caught up raised a dagger. A flash of cold light cut across my vision.

A sharp pain ripped through my abdomen. He drove the dagger in viciously. Blood burst out. I stared up at the pitch-black sky and slowly collapsed into the reeking gutter.

Tears blurred my sight.

Just like Elijah wanted, I was about to die.

But he didn’t know something else would die with me—another little life, stabbed through by that single knife, a secret I’d never gotten the chance to tell him.

I used to imagine how Elijah would react when he found out I was pregnant with his child—how happy, how wild with joy he’d be. Now I knew it had all been my fantasy. He treated my sincerity like dirt; how could he ever care about a poor nobody carrying his baby?

Going to heaven together with me… maybe that was better.

A thin comfort settled in my chest. I didn’t fight the thug at all. I stared at the night sky and used my last fading awareness to pray—if there was another life, don’t let me ever meet that heartless, cruel man again.

But when I regained awareness, my soul was being pulled—dragged—straight to Elijah.

It had already been three days since I died.

The newly built Foster Tower was holding its ribbon-cutting ceremony.

A Rolls-Royce drove up and stopped at the entrance to the plaza. Black-clad bodyguards jogged over, bent low, and opened the back door with reverence, inviting Elijah to step out.

Reporters already packed the area.

The moment that radiant man got out of the car, flashes erupted at once, a sea of light.

Under all those eyes, the kingly aura on Elijah only grew heavier, more overpowering, like he stood above everything. His impossibly handsome face was set in a cold, forbidding darkness.

This was nothing like the man who’d pretended to be broke just to toy with me.

Back then, he always smiled. He seemed approachable, warm as spring.

In the end, it turned out the smile had been a knife.

Even as a drifting soul, I still shuddered. With his real face revealed, the brutal chill pouring off him was terrifying. Even in death, fear swept over my heart.

I didn’t know why my awakened soul had been brought in front of him.

He walked toward me.

The man came closer.

Chapter 2 The Entertainment of High Society
I turned on instinct, ready to leave—when a familiar voice stopped me cold.

“Are you Elijah?” The words carried that careful, cramped politeness of someone who knew she didn’t belong.

I looked back.

It was my mother—Helen Harper.

It had only been three days since I’d last seen her, but half her hair had already gone white, the gray threaded through the black like a cruel joke. She wasn’t even fifty, yet she looked like an exhausted old woman who’d been wrung dry by life.

Elijah had definitely heard her. He only shifted slightly, his gaze sliding over my mother with a chill so detached it stung, and then he lengthened his stride and kept walking.

He didn’t know my mother.

Mom panicked and hurried after him. “Mr. Foster, you know my daughter, Yasmine, right?”

I froze.

Why was she bringing me up?

She came to find Elijah… because of me?

But I was already dead. What did I have to do with him anymore?

And yet—my name made him stop.

He turned slowly to face her. His eyes were iced over, and the slight curve of his mouth held not even a trace of warmth. It wasn’t a smile. It was the kind of contempt a man at the top used when he looked down at someone beneath him.

“I don’t.” His reply was cold and final.

My heart felt like it had been slammed onto a board of nails—punctured and shredded from every angle.

The man I’d worked multiple jobs for, just to save his life… said he didn’t know me.

Mom went still too, like she hadn’t expected that answer. She didn’t press him. Instead, tears spilled out, and she choked on her words.

“Mr. Foster… Yas has been missing for three days. Do you know where she is?”

Her tone was careful, almost pleading, but Elijah gave her nothing. He called over his assistant.

“Zach. Give this lady the address of the police station. Or help her file a missing person report.”

His indifference made her cry harder.

“Mr. Foster, the police just found Yas’s phone. Her last call was to you. But they said they couldn’t reach you, so I came to ask… I’m sorry to bother you.

“Mr. Foster… what did Yas say to you in her last call?”

Elijah’s face didn’t change. He stood a head taller than my mother, looking down at her like she was nothing.

“I get countless calls every day. How would I know which one was your daughter’s?”

Mom stared at him through tears, stunned—like she never imagined someone could be that heartless.

Rage roared through me too. I clenched my fists and swung at him with everything I had.

But I was dead.

No matter how hard I hit, my punch went right through him—light as air, unable to touch him, unable to hurt him even a little. All I could do was watch as bodyguards surrounded him and escorted him to the ribbon-cutting.

My mother stood there, and the guests passing by laughed at her.

“Honestly, these days anyone thinks they can come claim connections.”

“Look how cheap she’s dressed. Another one trying to sell her daughter, probably.”

“Disgusting.”

“The ribbon-cutting’s about to start. All unrelated people need to leave.” A security guard walked over and shoved my mom.

She was so thin. She stumbled twice, then fell hard to the ground.

I rushed to help her up—only for my body to pass straight through hers.

Not far away, the ceremony began. Elijah held a pair of gold scissors, and under a wave of applause and congratulations, he cut through the red ribbon.

Cameras flashed. Reporters snapped photo after photo.

Around him were nothing but flattering faces and eager praise.

Elijah stood there cold and distant, untouchable like a god.

And my mother lay on the ground, small as an ant.

She looked up at his dazzling, extraordinary figure, and her voice trembled as she whispered, “Yas… someone that precious… how could she ever love you? Back then you wouldn’t listen to your mother.”

I couldn’t hold it in anymore. I dropped to my knees in front of her, sobbing until my tears felt endless.

“Mom… I was wrong. I was wrong.”

When Elijah hid who he was and dated me, I once sent Mom a photo of him.

She’d seen his stunning face. Even dressed shabby, his bearing was unmistakable. She told me then, “Yas, he’s not ordinary. You won’t be able to keep him.”

After all, she had once been a society wife herself. She could read people sharply.

She warned me not to love too deeply.

But I didn’t listen. I threw everything I had into Elijah—every ounce of my feelings, all at once.

Mom struggled up helplessly. She lifted her phone and typed in a string of numbers. She hesitated for a long time… but she didn’t call.

Those eleven digits were my father’s number, but the two of them had been out of contact for years.

Mom must’ve wanted to beg my father for help. In the end, she went to file a report at the station.

And my soul—my wandering, useless soul—drifted back to Elijah again.

He was in a karaoke private room, drinking with a few rich boys.

I was dead, and he was celebrating.

On that handsome face, wild and indulgent, there wasn’t a single hint of sadness over my disappearance.

Glasses clinked back and forth. Then one man suddenly mentioned me.

“Eli, that Yasmine… you really not interested anymore?”

Elijah lounged back on the couch, one leg crossed over the other. His presence alone crushed the other men without effort. He swirled the red wine in his glass, his mouth curling in lazy disdain.

“Just something to play with. Not worth bringing up again. It kills the mood.”

Something to play with.

My floating soul jolted in midair.

I’d always known he looked down on me. But hearing that humiliating word out loud—so bare, so casual—still tore at me until it felt like my heart was being yanked apart.

“Exactly. Men, right? Who hasn’t slept with a few women? When you’re bored, you toss them.” Another man buttered Elijah up. “That woman’s just some broke nobody. She isn’t even worthy to carry Ms. Langley’s shoes. Why would our Eli waste a thought on her?”

“But she is pretty,” the first man said.

Elijah flicked his eyes over. “You want to sleep with her?”

The man stood, bent over, and poured Elijah more wine, grinning in a sleazy way. “That depends on what you say, Eli.”

“Do what you want.” Elijah’s face stayed cold, his answer without the slightest hesitation.

I sucked in a breath of icy air, and my heart sank all the way to the bottom.

This was the man I’d given everything to. The man I’d worked myself half-dead for, just to keep him alive. Not only was he cruel and indifferent—he turned me into entertainment for high society.

“Thanks, man.” The guy clinked his glass against Elijah’s, thrilled.

Like I was already his for the taking.

Only he didn’t know.

I was dead.

They couldn’t play with me anymore.

For some reason, Elijah didn’t drink the glass the man poured. He stayed silent, lit a cigarette, and after the first drag, the phone on the table rang.

Chapter 3: Believing Those Easy Words—“I Like You”
I saw the name on the screen.

“Vivi.”

My heart took another vicious hit.

Elijah had saved my number as Yasmine.

When I found out, I’d been annoyed and made him change it. “Elijah, put something like ‘wife’ or ‘baby’ or ‘sweetheart,’ okay? Using my name is so cold.”

Elijah had said, “Names are safer. Don’t you know how scams work now? They target contacts with special meanings. And don’t save my name as ‘husband’ or anything that exposes who I am. Be careful you don’t get tricked.”

Back then, I’d actually believed he was doing it for me.

Only now did I understand. A man who doesn’t love you won’t even spare you a nickname.

“Hello.” Elijah picked up. It was only one word, but his tone was unbelievably gentle. “...You don’t feel well... okay... I’m coming right now.”

He hung up and stood. “Vivienne doesn’t feel well. I’m going to check on her. Enjoy your drinks.”

He left cleanly, ignoring the way the other men tried to keep him there.

“Didn’t expect Eli to care that much about Vivienne.”

“Of course he does. Eli spent two hundred million dollars to win that diamond ring and propose to Vivienne. Who’d throw away that kind of money for someone they didn’t care about? You ever seen him spend anything on Yasmine? Not a cent. He even had that woman working like an idiot to earn money for him.”

“Honestly, she got played so hard. Back on that yacht, she got mocked until her face went white.” As the man spoke, he slung an arm over the shoulder of the guy who wanted to mess with me and grinned nastily. “Wesley Wells, when you finally get her, be generous to her, yeah?”

The man named Wesley gave a disdainful laugh. “A free toy like that is worth, what, one meal at most.”

“Hey, don’t say it like that. She was our boss’s woman, after all. That makes her your sister-in-law...”

Hahahaha.

In the sickening laughter of those men, my soul drifted to Elijah.

He was speeding to Vivienne.

I sat in the passenger seat and turned my head to look at him.

He was the most beautiful man I’d ever seen. Devastatingly handsome features—perfect from any angle.

Flawless.

And yet, that perfect face hid a heart that was cold and thin.

A deep sadness rose in me.

I had never once enjoyed the luxury of calling and having him come at once.

When I wanted to see him, he always said he was on a run, or he’d worked a night shift and needed sleep. Only when he had time would he come to me.

But one call from Vivienne, and he could drop his friends and leave.

So many details, so many moments that proved he didn’t love me—and I’d still missed them. I’d trusted the way he said he liked me, and I’d sunk in deep.

Vivienne was at a hotel.

She wore a black satin slip. Her breasts were half-exposed. The message couldn’t have been clearer—she was inviting Elijah to bed. No wonder she’d booked a room outside. So she could really let loose.

The fabric was semi-sheer. Her curves showed in and out of view, mysterious and seductive.

Her body really was... something.

The moment Elijah saw her, his throat moved slightly.

He walked over, lifted Vivienne’s chin with a light touch, and desire churned in his eyes. “Your stomach hurts and you’re still wearing something with a neckline that low?”

Vivienne pouted as she wrapped her arms around him. On the middle finger of her left hand, she wore the engagement diamond Elijah had spent two hundred million dollars to win. The oversized stone flashed a brilliant arc through the air—bright enough to stab straight into my eyes.

I’d always thought I was Elijah’s official girlfriend.

Turns out I was nothing but his entertainment.

He’d casually braided a little ring out of weeds and slipped it onto my middle finger, and with that, he stole my whole heart. For his one hundred thousand dollars in medical bills, I’d worked multiple jobs a day. I’d even sold blood.

And now, he could toss two hundred million dollars at someone else for a ring without blinking.

He cherished Vivienne like she was heaven.

He ground me into the dirt.

Vivienne rested against Elijah’s chest, small and helpless, like a little white rabbit. She said sweetly, “Elijah, you promised after the engagement you’d be with me. But it’s been three days, and you haven’t made a move. I had to be the one to bring you here.”

Then Vivienne lifted her face, looking at him with deep affection, cheeks shyly flushed. “Elijah, I want to give myself to you tonight.”

I froze in shock.

I hadn’t expected Elijah still hadn’t slept with Vivienne.

The air carried a faint rose scent. Beside them, an aroma lamp let out thin curls of smoke.

Rose essential oil—people said it could arouse you.

Facing a woman dressed this sexy, Elijah was clearly stirred. He lowered his head and took Vivienne’s earlobe into his mouth, sucking slowly, lingering.

Vivienne immediately let out a soft moan.

And pain tore through my chest.

This was Elijah’s favorite move.

When he was with me, he’d loved kissing and sucking my earlobe too. That gentle, wet warmth could make me excited so fast.

He’d even told me my earlobe was soft and fleshy, that it felt good to kiss.

But now he was kissing another woman’s earlobe, his face lost in it.

Vivienne melted under Elijah’s tenderness, turning weak and liquid. Before anything even really started, she was already making one breathy sound after another—enough to make anyone’s blood boil.

Elijah lifted her up, ready to carry her to the bed—

and his phone rang.

He paused mid-step.

Vivienne instantly clung to his neck and kissed his lips on her own. “Eli, I want...”

Her voice was pure temptation. But Elijah still set her down, then kissed her cheek like a consolation prize. “Let me take this call first.”

He saw a short text prompt on the screen, letting him know it was the police.

Elijah picked up his phone and walked to the window to answer. “Hello.”

“Is this Mr. Elijah?”

“I am.”

“Hello, Mr. Foster. This is the Millbrook Police Station.” Speaking to someone important, the officer’s tone was polite. “Sorry to disturb you so late, Mr. Foster, but there’s a small case. We need you to come to the station.”

The police station.

Elijah’s face darkened, the interruption written in cold lines. “What do you need to ask me?”

After the officer handed Elijah a cup of tea, he spoke respectfully, “Mr. Foster, it’s like this. Recently, we received a missing person report.

The missing person is named Yasmine. We found her phone near Clearwater Bay. The last call Yasmine made was to you, Mr. Foster...”

“I think my assistant already explained this to you.” Elijah cut him off, icy and impatient. “Why are you still calling me in?”

The officer hurried to say, “Yes, Mr. Foster. Zachary explained it to us at the time. But we just restored the data on Yasmine’s phone, and in her photo album, we found pictures of you and Yasmine together.

That should prove you know Yasmine...”

“What pictures?” Elijah interrupted again, his voice razor-cold. “Bed photos?”

Chapter 4: She Saved Two Venomous Snakes
The cop froze for a second, then muttered, “No… no, it’s not that. It’s just a normal photo.”

Elijah hooked his lips into a cold smile. “I’m a public figure. I’ve taken photos with plenty of people. If something happens to every one of them, does it all have to be tied to me?”

The cop didn’t have much to say after that.

I hung in the air and let out a dry little laugh.

Now I finally understood why Elijah never took intimate photos with me. He’d been scared that later, I’d use them to cling to him.

That photo the police found was the only selfie Elijah and I ever took together.

I was beaming at the camera. Elijah’s smile didn’t reach his eyes. It looked exactly like a fan posing with her idol—there wasn’t even a hint of closeness.

This man left behind not a single trace that I’d ever been tangled up with him.

With that level of caution… how was I supposed to outplay him?

“But Yasmine has been missing for several days,” the cop said. “We’re just following procedure, looking for related clues. We hope Mr. Foster can understand.”

Elijah’s voice dropped. “She has nothing to do with me.”

Heh.

How heartless did you have to be to say something that cruel?

I died carrying his child, and he still dared to say I had nothing to do with him!

“It’s all my fault.” Vivienne suddenly started crying at his side, all sobs and sniffles.

She was sitting right next to Elijah. The moment he saw the woman he loved crying, Elijah immediately reached over, pulled her in by the shoulder, and asked gently, “What’s wrong?”

Vivienne choked back tears, guilt all over her face. “Elijah, that day on the yacht… I shouldn’t have accepted your engagement ring. I hurt my sister. But I really didn’t know you and my sister were dating. If I’d known sooner, I would’ve backed out.

“My sister was so heartbroken that day. Watching her… it hurt me too…”

Vivienne’s voice broke off. Tears fell one by one, making her look painfully pitiful.

Floating above her head, I sneered.

This woman’s best talent was pretending to be a wounded little bunny so men would pity her. But I knew the truth.

She was a genuine, textbook fake bitch.

Before I turned ten, I was a wealthy heiress too. It was only after my mom let wolves into the house that I became, in Elijah’s words, an ant living at the very bottom of society.

Vivienne had originally been the daughter of my father’s driver. After a car accident, Vivienne’s father died, leaving Vivienne and her mother, Shannon Fitzgerald, clinging to each other.

My mother was soft-hearted. She pitied the widow and child, took them into the Turner home, and even adopted Vivienne—treating her like her own.

Who would’ve thought those two would repay kindness with betrayal?

Shannon used her pretty face to seduce my father, Logan Turner. When my mother discovered their disgusting affair, she asked for a divorce. Logan, of course, refused. He was the one at fault, and Mom would take a huge chunk of his assets.

But my mother’s heart had gone cold for real. In the end, she chose to walk away with nothing. Only then did Logan agree to the divorce.

She took me and left the Turner family behind, cutting off contact with Logan, and raised me on her own.

Vivienne, meanwhile, transformed overnight into the wealthy heiress.

And I—once the rich girl—became Cinderella.

One time, right after I’d separated from Elijah, I ran into Vivienne.

She gave me a twisted little smile and said, “Sis, your boyfriend is so handsome. You’d better put some effort into keeping a tight hold on him.”

She’d clearly seen me with Elijah. How could she possibly not know we were together?

She just played along with Elijah, acting out that whole performance of messing with me. And even when Elijah ruthlessly threw the pills I’d bought by selling my blood—one by one—onto the floor, she still kept acting.

She panicked and crouched to pick them up, pleading anxiously, “Elijah, stop throwing them. Let my sister take the meds to resell and get some living money. Their family is so poor right now…”

Every word she spoke was loaded and cutting, yet everyone around us heard nothing but her ‘kindness.’

She wore sorrow on her face, but when her eyes met mine, they were filled with the sick satisfaction of finally seeing me humiliated—exactly like the day my mom and I left the Turner family with nothing, when she leaned close and whispered in my ear.

“Big sister… everything you had is finally all mine.”

But in the next breath, she turned toward everyone with reddened eyes and tears, choking out in heartbreak, “Sis, I’m sorry. This is the adults’ business—I can’t interfere. But from now on, if you ever have any difficulties, just tell me. I’ll help you with everything I’ve got.”

That fake ingénue stole my identity, my status, and my wealth.

My mom had been kind… and ended up like a farmer who saved two venomous snakes.

Hearing Vivienne, Elijah lightly wiped her tears away, his gaze full of indulgence. “Don’t cry over someone who doesn’t matter.”

Doesn’t matter…

Those words had already stabbed me so many times, I’d gone numb.

“But she’s my adopted sister,” Vivienne said, worry rising on her face. “When we were little and lived together at the Turner house, she was really good to me. Is she truly missing?”

Elijah’s voice turned icy. “Weeds are lowly but hard to kill. Don’t waste your concern.”

“I guess.” Vivienne’s grief eased a little, her tone turning superficially light. “My sister was like this when she was little too. If she got unhappy, she’d play disappearing and make everyone go looking for her.

“I remember one time we couldn’t find her, and Dad was so anxious he almost called the police. But then my sister suddenly came back, like nothing had happened.

“This time, I think she’s probably just throwing a little tantrum again—trying to make you go find her.

“Sigh… my sister just has a bit of a temper. She’s actually pretty kind.”

Hearing her bring that up made me want to tear that manipulative bitch’s face apart.

That time, she was the one who locked me in the attic and wouldn’t let me out. I was locked up for days. If there hadn’t been some dry food stored up there, I would’ve starved.

That day I was locked in, Logan had been planning to take me to a city government banquet. I was supposed to go onstage and perform. But I disappeared. With no other choice, he took Vivienne to the banquet instead.

She danced in my place.

Not only did she protect the Turner family’s reputation, she also helped my father land a major project—letting Logan make a fortune.

And compared to that, I—the one who ‘vanished for no reason’—looked spoiled and selfish beyond belief.

So Logan liked her even more.

Logan had never been close to me. After that, he grew even more distant. I used to think he just preferred sons and didn’t like that I was a girl. Businessmen always want a son to inherit.

But seeing how much he adored Vivienne, I finally understood.

It wasn’t that he didn’t like daughters.

He just didn’t like me—his daughter who couldn’t charm people in every direction.

And Vivienne did everything she could to please the Turner family. She had a sweet mouth, she was slick, and she won people over easily.

Everyone thought she was more refined than me, more gentle, more kind.

Once Vivienne gained the Turner family’s approval, she started coming after me openly, setting up situation after situation to make it look like I bullied her. Every time she succeeded. Every time I couldn’t defend myself. Little by little, I became the “vicious older sister.”

Even later, when I exposed that Vivienne was the one who locked me in the attic, no one believed me.

The adopted daughter was held up and adored, while I—the real wealthy heiress—was despised. I was too young to handle that kind of whiplash, so I’d hide and cry in secret.

When the family couldn’t find me, they’d say I was throwing a tantrum and playing disappearing.

That reputation—me always vanishing—spread like wildfire.

But the truth was, it was all just a label Vivienne slapped on me.

The cop caught something in her story and turned to Vivienne. “Ms. Langley, what’s your relationship with Yasmine?”

Chapter 5: Taking My Life Over a Man?
"Yasmine is my adopted older sister. She used to be the Turner family’s Young Madam. My current father, Logan, is my sister’s biological father." Vivienne spoke lightly, like she was chatting over coffee. "My sister may not live with the Turners anymore, but she used to be a wealthy heiress. That spoiled personality is probably carved into her bones. She still can’t change it.

When we were kids, Dad liked me more than he liked her, so my sister would ‘go missing’ all the time just to get his attention. When she saw everyone panicking and searching for her, she’d be happy. Satisfied.

After a while, it became a habit. The second she was upset, she’d disappear. Then a few days later she’d come back perfectly fine. Everyone would be half-dead from worry, and she’d act like nothing happened.

This time, she’s definitely just in a bad mood and playing the disappearing act again. She just wants Elijah to go looking for her."

As Vivienne spoke, she squeezed Elijah’s hand, like meeting me had wronged him in the worst way.

Elijah’s face stayed cold, unreadable.

But I was so furious my vision almost blurred. I wanted to slap this fake ingénue across the face.

What kind of shamelessness did it take to frame someone so calmly, without even blinking?

The entire Turner family was blind, fooled by her sweet, rotten act.

The cop looked doubtful. "Is that so?"

Vivienne asked, "Other than the phone, you didn’t find any other leads, right?"

"Not at the moment," the cop said.

"Exactly." Vivienne sighed. "She dropped her phone on purpose, left a little clue, just to make everyone worry.

I really didn’t expect that after all these years, she still hasn’t grown out of this disappearing habit.

But she’ll come back."

The cop frowned. "Why are you so sure?"

Vivienne smiled. "Because in a few days it’s Great-Grandpa’s ninetieth birthday banquet. Our Turner family is throwing a big, glamorous party. Great-Grandpa loves my sister the most—his oldest great-granddaughter. No matter how much she pouts, she’ll come back to celebrate his birthday."

Tears fell from me without warning.

Vivienne wasn’t wrong. In the Turner family, the one who loved me most was Great-Grandpa.

This fake ingénue stole everything from me—but she never stole my place in Great-Grandpa’s heart. Too bad he was already so old. He loved me, but sometimes he was clear, sometimes he was confused. When it came to the younger generation’s mess, he was powerless.

A few days ago, when he was lucid, he called me and talked about his birthday.

"Yas, Great-Grandpa lives one day at a time. This might be the last time I get to celebrate a full birthday.

You have to come back and celebrate with me."

"Okay, Great-Grandpa. I’ll definitely come back to celebrate you," I’d promised.

But now… I was going to break that promise.

I was already dead. I could never go back to wish him happy birthday.

"She’s probably hiding somewhere, watching everyone run around in circles for her," Vivienne added viciously. "She’s probably secretly thrilled."

After listening to Vivienne’s whole performance, Elijah stood up. "Crimes happen every day. I hope the police don’t waste resources on a spoiled young lady’s boring game.

And certainly not my time.

This Ms. Turner has nothing to do with me."

Seeing how cold he was, the cop didn’t say much more. "Alright. We’ll contact the Turner family and investigate."

"On Great-Grandpa’s birthday banquet day, my sister will definitely come back." As they left the station, Vivienne reassured Elijah again, so confident it sounded like a vow.

But after Elijah drove Vivienne home, he stayed alone in the car for a long time.

He picked up his phone again and again. In the end, he narrowed his eyes and said harshly, "Yasmine, you’d better not show up at that banquet."

He looked vicious, like if I showed up, it would mean his worry had been wasted—and he’d strangle me for it.

Fine.

I wouldn’t disappoint him.

I was dead. I couldn’t possibly appear at Great-Grandpa’s birthday banquet two days later.

And yet—when my soul opened its eyes, I was at the banquet resort.

Maybe heaven took pity on me, letting me wish Great-Grandpa happy birthday one last time.

The resort was lit up and decorated, packed with guests. Loud. Festive.

Ninety was a milestone birthday. Of course the Turner family had to throw it big.

I floated in the air, watching Great-Grandpa in his traditional tunic, kind-faced and gentle. Warmth filled me… and so did grief.

I never expected that phone call would be my goodbye.

Great-Grandpa sat in a grand rosewood armchair. One by one, the younger generations came forward to wish him longevity.

When it was the great-grandchildren’s turn, it was Vivienne who carried the tea over to celebrate him.

She replaced me again—me, the oldest great-granddaughter.

And Elijah stood right beside her, the most powerful man in the city. It made Vivienne glow with pride. The diamond ring on her hand—worth two hundred million dollars—sparkled so brightly it practically blinded everyone.

"So beautiful. I’ve never seen a rock that big."

"Young Master Foster is really generous with our Vivienne."

"Vivienne’s gorgeous and capable. She’s the queen of the socialite circle, and Mr. Foster is the king of the big shots. They’re made for each other. Of course Young Master Foster treats her sincerely."

"Even though she’s adopted, she’s more impressive than a real heiress."

"Adopted? Vivienne is the Turner family’s real young lady. The Turner family’s pride.

That real heiress is nothing…"

The room buzzed with praise for Vivienne.

And all I ever received was contempt.

The Turners treated Elijah with extreme courtesy, practically worshiping him as an honored guest. Especially Logan—he kept shaking Elijah’s hand and wouldn’t let go, smiling so hard his face almost cracked. "Young Master Foster, your presence at Great-Grandpa’s birthday banquet really adds so much glory to the whole event."

If it were only the Turner family, their wealth and status in front of Elijah didn’t even count as small fries.

With Vivienne engaged to Elijah, the Turners had finally latched onto a true top-tier family.

"Chairman Turner, you flatter me." After a few bland pleasantries with Logan, Elijah presented Great-Grandpa with his gift. "Happy birthday, Great-Grandpa. May the sun and moon shine bright for you; may you live long and strong. May you always smile, surrounded by family."

Great-Grandpa accepted it happily. "Thank you, Young Master Foster."

Next, it was Vivienne’s turn to offer tea.

Holding the teacup, she knelt in front of Great-Grandpa. "Great-Grandpa, your great-granddaughter Vivienne wishes you endless blessings and a long life."

Great-Grandpa had been smiling, but when he saw it was Vivienne wishing him well, surprise flickered across his face. "Why is it you? Where’s Yas? She promised she’d come celebrate my birthday."

He didn’t take the tea. He lifted his head, searching the crowd. When he didn’t see me, his joyful expression darkened in an instant.

"Did you not let Yas in?" Great-Grandpa’s tone turned sharp.

Even though he no longer ran Turner Enterprises, in the family he still held the highest status.

The moment he got angry, the entire atmosphere turned colder.

Standing to the side was the Old Madam—my grandmother, Georgia Wells. She frowned, clearly displeased. "What, the police still haven’t found that dead girl?"

Her words dripped with disgust. One sentence was enough to prove she never liked me.

But from that line, I could tell the police must have already called the Turners and asked about me.

After all, Vivienne had explained my relationship with the family. The police had to go through procedure.

And yet Georgia’s tone also made something else painfully clear.

No one cared about my disappearance.

Two more days had passed, and not a single person had called the police again to ask if I’d been found.

I’d been missing for five days.

My body should’ve already started to stink.

"Police?" Great-Grandpa’s face changed drastically. He turned to Logan beside him. "Logan, what’s going on?"

"Grandpa, don’t worry. That girl is just throwing a tantrum…" The man in a crisp suit brushed it off, lightly describing my disappearance.

The tone he used was like he was talking about a stranger.

"She just went out of town to clear her head. She’ll be back in a few days. Grandpa, don’t be so worried."

"That girl’s had a temper since she was little. She pulled this disappearing act once as a kid too—didn’t show up for days. Everyone was panicking like crazy, and she came back acting like nothing happened."

The one stepping on me was my aunt, Judith Turner.

Insulting me wasn’t enough. She had to praise Vivienne too. "And it was that time she almost ruined my big brother’s project. Luckily Vivienne saved the day. Otherwise the Turner family would’ve lost a huge deal.

Vivienne is beautiful and talented. If Yasmine were even half as capable, she’d bring the Turners some pride."

"Please. Forget bringing pride. It’d be good enough if she didn’t embarrass the family." The voice came from Jennifer, Uncle James’s wife. "I heard she’s been working at a club lately…"

She didn’t finish before Georgia cut her off. "What day is it? Don’t bring up filthy things."

It was Great-Grandpa’s milestone birthday. So many guests. She hated me, but she didn’t want to air dirty laundry in public.

Jennifer shut up.

"What club?" Great-Grandpa had heard it anyway. His voice dropped, heavy with anger. "What kind of filth are you smearing on Yas?"

"Grandpa, Yasmine is your favorite. Who would dare smear her?" Judith hurried to smooth things over. Seeing Vivienne still kneeling, she reminded him, "Grandpa, Vivienne’s arms are getting tired. Just take the tea already."

"That’s right. Drink Vivienne’s longevity tea." Second Uncle James chimed in. "Yasmine is just throwing a little fit. It’s not worth getting angry over."

Great-Grandpa suddenly looked at Vivienne. Angry, he lifted his hand and pointed his cane at her, scolding, "Vivienne—did you hide Yas again?"

Elijah, who’d been silent the whole time, lifted a brow.

Chapter 6: How Could He Miss Me?
Vivienne’s face flashed with shock. She shook her head fast. “Great-Grandpa, how could I hide my sister—”

Great-Grandpa cut her off. “Last time, it was you who locked Yas in the attic and made everyone think she was throwing a tantrum and hiding on purpose. You lied to Yas, lured her up there, and locked her in, just so you could steal her chance to perform at City Hall.

“This time, what kind of scheme are you playing now?”

Great-Grandpa demanded, furious.

Vivienne looked innocent and terrified. Her eyes reddened in an instant. Even the hands holding her teacup were trembling. “Great-Grandpa, it wasn’t me.”

“Dad, don’t be mad. Why bring up old stuff?” Georgia hurried to support Great-Grandpa. “Vivienne is so sweet and well-behaved. How could it possibly be her who locked that dead girl in the attic?

“Don’t go believing rumors.”

“It was her!” Great-Grandpa glared at Vivienne. “Yas told me herself. You locked her in the attic. Other people don’t believe it, but I do.”

My eyes burned hot.

Great-Grandpa was so angry he suddenly jabbed his cane down onto the cup.

The cup fell to the floor and shattered. Tea splashed all over Vivienne.

I saw it—so fast it was almost nothing—a cold glint sliding through Vivienne’s eyes. But she pretended to shake in fear, tears spilling as she whimpered, “Great-Grandpa, it really wasn’t me.”

That pitiful, delicate look made Logan ache for her. He immediately stepped in to protect Vivienne. “Grandpa, Vivienne has been good and sensible since she was a kid. How could she lock Yasmine in the attic? You can’t just listen to one side.

“Yasmine’s always had a temper. She plays disappearance games—”

“Shut up!” Great-Grandpa lifted his cane and struck Logan across the back. “No matter how much Yas throws a tantrum, she would never skip my birthday banquet. Something must’ve happened to her—that’s the only reason she broke her word.

“Logan, Yas is your daughter. Don’t let your mind get clogged with grease and end up pitying the wrong person.

“Get to the police station right now and find out what’s going on with Yas.”

Great-Grandpa barked the order.

Seeing the Old Master truly furious, Logan answered again and again, “Yes, yes, Grandpa. I’m going right now.”

Logan left the longevity hall. Georgia immediately lowered her voice to Elijah. “Young Master Foster, the Old Master’s a little confused. Please don’t take it to heart.”

“Yes, yes. After all, he’s ninety,” Uncle James chimed in.

They were terrified Elijah would believe it, form a bad impression of Vivienne, and ruin the engagement.

Elijah said nothing, his attitude unreadable.

Vivienne lowered her head and cried softly, looking wronged. At a time like this, acting innocent was stronger than anything she could say.

After Logan went out, he didn’t go to the police station at all. He called his assistant over and told him to pass a message to my mom. “Tell Helen to find Yasmine right away. Tell her not to cause trouble for the Turner family!”

Trouble.

So I was his trouble.

I’d known for a long time I didn’t matter in his heart, but hearing those words out loud still hurt like hell.

In the entire Turner family, only Great-Grandpa had ever truly loved me.

I knelt on the floor and knocked my head three times, hard.

I’m sorry, Great-Grandpa. I can’t stay alive to wish you longevity, but you have to live a long, long life.

It was like Great-Grandpa felt my blessing. He lifted his head and looked toward where I was kneeling, his eyes turning wet. He sighed, propping himself up with his cane. “All of you… you’re all blind.”

Then he pointed at Vivienne, still kneeling on the floor. “If you dare stir up trouble again, heaven will take you. Keep kneeling.”

Vivienne bit her lip lightly, wearing the obedient, dutiful face of someone falsely accused yet not daring to argue.

But her eyes were dark with chill.

She’d brought Elijah here to celebrate longevity, wanting to show off in front of the guests. Instead, Great-Grandpa had smashed the teacup and punished her on her knees.

Great-Grandpa had no mood to accept any more birthday wishes. He left the longevity hall.

The guests followed. After everyone dispersed, Elijah finally helped Vivienne up.

Vivienne sniffled softly and looked at Elijah with wounded eyes. “Elijah… do you not believe me either?”

Elijah paused, then looked at her. “That day at the police station, you were so sure Yasmine would come back. But today she didn’t.”

Vivienne hurried to explain, “I don’t know why she didn’t come back either. Great-Grandpa loves her most. Logically, she would definitely come back to wish him a happy birthday. But she’s still being stubborn. This time, my sister really has no sense of boundaries.

“Even if she’s heartbroken from a breakup, she can’t let Great-Grandpa down.”

I narrowed my eyes.

What a fake ingénue. Even while scrubbing herself clean, she still found time to splash a bucket of filth all over me.

Elijah didn’t speak.

Vivienne hooked her arm through his. “Elijah, don’t worry about my sister for now. She’s probably just too hurt, hiding a little longer this time. The banquet’s starting. Let’s go over. You’re the main guest, and later you have to go onstage to give Great-Grandpa a birthday speech.”

Elijah lifted his lips. The word “okay” hadn’t even left his mouth when his phone rang.

After glancing at the caller ID showing the police station, Elijah answered. “Hello.”

“Hello, Mr. Foster. This is Officer Walters from the Millbrook Police Station. There’s a new development in Yasmine’s case. It’s somewhat related to you. Mr. Foster, could you come to the station and cooperate with the investigation?”

“Sure,” Elijah agreed, crisp and immediate.

A cold gleam flashed through Vivienne’s eyes, but her voice stayed sweet with concern. “Is there new progress in my sister’s case?”

Elijah didn’t hide it. “Yeah. I’m heading to the station now.”

“I’ll go with you.”

Elijah refused at first. “I’ll handle the case. The banquet is about to start. You stay and eat with Great-Grandpa, or he’ll get unhappy again.”

“Elijah, you saw it. Great-Grandpa is really worried about my sister. If I go handle my sister’s situation, he won’t be unhappy.” Vivienne’s face was full of concern. “And I’m worried about her too. I want to know what new clues the police found.”

At the police station.

I drifted into the reception room ahead of Vivienne and Elijah.

I saw my cousin, Cameron Shaw. He was telling the officer, “My aunt is sick and can’t get out of bed. I came in her place. Officer, what’s the new lead?”

My heart clenched.

I’d been missing for five days. Mom must’ve been so devastated she’d gotten sick.

“We’ll go look once Mr. Foster arrives,” the officer said.

Cameron’s tone turned heavy. “Does the clue have something to do with Elijah?”

“It’s a little…” The officer stopped mid-sentence and smiled, nodding toward behind Cameron. “Mr. Foster, you’re here.”

Cameron turned around.

Vivienne had her arm linked with Elijah’s, the two of them walking in as a pair.

Seeing that sick display of closeness, Cameron’s face instantly darkened with rage. He strode up in a few big steps, stopping right in front of Elijah. “Elijah, you sanctimonious hypocrite! Yas gave you everything, and this is how you treat her!

“When she comes back, you will apologize to her!”

Elijah let out a cold laugh, mocking Cameron’s anger like it was nothing but cheap posturing. They were both tall, solid men, but Elijah’s shadow covered Cameron with a pressure that felt born into his bones.

“Want me to apologize to her?” Elijah’s voice was icy. “Then let her crawl to my feet and beg for forgiveness first.”

My heart ripped in two.

I’d been good to him in every way. I even sold my blood to buy him medicine—and I still had to beg him for forgiveness?
